title: Morrisons becomes one of first UK grocery brands to tap autonomous delivery as Just Eat expands trial
key_facts: Just Eat is expanding its autonomous delivery robot trial with Starship Technologies to Cambourne in Cambridgeshire, the first trial location where it does not already offer grocery delivery; it builds on deployments in Sunderland and Milton Keynes.

Morrisons has become one of the first grocery brands to use the technology; the Cambourne supermarket, now live, is the fourth Morrisons to begin autonomous robot deliveries, after three Morrisons Daily stores in Sunderland and Milton Keynes.
Stated benefits include extra delivery capacity in the run-up to the festive season and during offers such as the regular 'Half Price Wednesdays' on Just Eat.
Morrisons' Charlotte Exell says shoppers ordering from the Cambourne store through the app will have their orders delivered exclusively by robot.

Just Eat's Caroline Bates says the trials aim to improve the customer experience, enabling delivery in new areas like Cambourne or more capacity and speed before Christmas, and that Just Eat will listen closely to customer feedback.
Starship Technologies' David Ringer says its robots are built for reliability and to make the grocery shop convenient and fast.
No figures on deliveries, speed or customer response were given.
